name: Alaska-Aleutian subduction zone, Shumagin segment

fault_trace.comment: APPROXIMATE, hand-digitized reference line (Alaska Peninsula coast near the Shumagin Islands), NOT survey-grade -- same caveat as Cascadia: no lightweight open trench/slab-geometry service found in this session, proxy uses the onshore coast where GNSS stations and recorded crustal/interface seismicity actually are. Anchors: near Chignik, AK (56.30,-158.40) to near Sand Point, AK (55.34,-160.50). CHOSEN because it ruptured in a real, well-documented M7.8+M7.6 doublet on 2020-07-22/2020-10-19 (broke part of a gap unruptured since 1917) -- unlike Cascadia (locked, no comparable instrumental-era rupture), this segment gives real large target events plus documented along-strike coupling variability (creeping west, coupled east) in the same corridor.

corridor_comment: Wider than California segments -- subduction interface seismicity/deformation footprint is broader than a single strike-slip trace, and the 2020 doublet ruptured a multi-segment patch.

gnss.fault_azimuth_comment: approximate, roughly WSW-ENE following the Aleutian arc trend in this sector

state.v_ref_comment: Pacific-North America convergence at the Alaska-Aleutian trench is much faster than Cascadia/California -- placeholder pending real calibration against published coupling models
state.recurrence_source: Shumagin gap: no large (M~7.4+) interface rupture 1917-2020 (103yr gap, motivating decades of 'seismic gap' literature -- Davies et al. 1981 and follow-ups). PARTIALLY RUPTURED 2020-07-22 (M7.8) + 2020-10-19 (M7.6) doublet -- eastern segment broke, western segment reportedly still creeping/less coupled per recent geodetic studies. T_rec/years_since_last here describe the PRE-2020 gap, not a clean post-2020 reset (the doublet did not rupture the whole historical gap) -- treat C_state for this segment as the least clean interpretation of all 4 segments so far, flag explicitly whenever used.

etas_lite.target_mag_comment: Higher than California segments -- subduction-zone background rate at M4.5 would be dominated by routine intraslab/outer-rise seismicity unrelated to the interface coupling this segment is meant to characterize; 5.5 keeps focus on interface-relevant events while still catching the 2020 doublet and its aftershock sequence.
etas_lite.train_end_comment: Earlier cutoff than other segments -- deliberately keeps the 2020 doublet + aftershocks in the HOLDOUT window, since that's the one genuinely large, well-documented rupture this segment offers.
